content.title: Is Bill Murray a UConn fan? Why famous actor is attending March Madness games for Huskies
content.text: Where does Luke Bryan live? The American Idol judge was born in Georgia but now resides on a sprawling farm just outside Nashville, Tennessee—the natural choice for a country superstar with over 30 number-one hits under his belt. Back in 2020, he told AD about his penchant for neoclassical style home “with the big columns,” and his love of more traditional furniture. “Your rocking chairs have to match; your antique dressers have to actually be antique,” he said. Bryan hired Nashville designer Chad James to imbue his 150-acre farm with that southern sensibility, custom-building a 10,000-square-foot mansion, a three-bedroom guesthouse, and a massive party barn on the rural property. When the musician added a Florida vacation home to his real estate portfolio, he hired James to bring his tried-and-true country style to that beachside oasis as well. Read on to learn more about the places that the “Buy Dirt” singer has called home. Former Tennessee home Nashville-area farm In 2012, Bryan bought a sprawling Tennessee farm—a lifelong dream for the musician. “Everything there is Caroline’s and my brainchild,” he told AD in 2020, referring to his wife. “We took 150 acres of cow pasture and turned it into something we couldn’t be more proud of. As a child, one of my biggest dreams was to own a lake to fish on. I thought that if I could ever have a home that sits on a bass lake, that’s all I would ever need to grow old and gray. Once we found out that the property could have a bass lake, we built one.” Throughout the property, the singer incorporated the rocks that had been excavated while building the lake. “We had 140 tons, maybe more, of rock, and since that area of Tennessee is really known for its Civil War stone fences, we replicated a lot of that with the rock we excavated from the lake,” he explained. “We also created fireplaces and our sunken courtyard with it.” Located in Williamson County outside of Nashville, the farm—named Red Bird in honor of Bryan’s late sister—has three main structures, which were custom-built with the help of interior designer Chad James: a 10,000-square-foot main house, a 1,800-square-foot guesthouse, and a 7,000-square-foot party barn. “We trash the barn and leave the house alone,” Bryan explained of the latter. “The barn also has these unique cobblestone floors. They’re great barometers of how much you’ve had to drink. If you fall on the cobblestones, you’ve had too many. I have a golf simulator and kegerator in there, and it’s where I smoke my cigars.” While the main home was being built, the Bryans stayed in the guesthouse, which features three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a double-height living room with a stone fireplace, a media room, a kitchen, and a screened-in porch. Outside the structure, a path leads to a catfish pond. In contrast, little is known about the farm’s main house, which now serves as the “Country Girl” singer’s primary residence. Florida beach house In 2013, Bryan bought a sunny slice of Florida real estate, paying $2.5 million for a contemporary-style five-bedroom, five-bathroom Santa Rosa Beach house. The 4,645-square-foot home sat on an acre with 95 feet of Gulf frontage. The singer again tapped James as his designer, appointing the space with a casual coastal style. “We spend a month or so there every year, and it really is a beach house. When you walk in, nothing feels like a museum or prim and proper,” Bryan said of the property in a 2020 interview with AD. “But that’s how we want it. We want the house to be fun and chilled-out.” Bryan also hired architect Geoff Chick to reconfigure the home’s layout and add a fourth story to incorporate more room for guests, plus an entertainment room. Throughout the home, views of the water were emphasized, with a seaside-inspired palette further blending the interiors with their scenic locale. Pine floors reclaimed from a Georgia factory lent the residence a lived-in country patina, while Pennsylvania Dutch barn beams crowned the living room ceiling. “This is where Luke and I can actually relax and not run 100 miles per hour,” Caroline told Traditional Home for a 2017 tour. “Typically, all five kids are here with us. There is nothing better. And Luke can fish all day, which makes him the happiest man on the Gulf.” Expansive porches are attached to each level, while a terrace with a swimming pool and barbecue area abuts the house, overlooking the beach. The home was dubbed Snowman in honor of Bryan’s late brother, Chris, who earned the nickname from the golf slang for a score of eight on an individual hole. “Evidently, Chris wasn’t a great golfer,” Caroline explained. “Snowman became his nickname. We named our farm Red Bird Farm after Luke’s sister and wanted to honor Chris as well.” Bryan no longer owns this residence; the Georgia native first listed the home for $18 million in 2022, but it wasn’t until several price slashes that the place finally sold in 2024 for $11.5 million.
